messages:
Alexa (PM): quick sync — we need to pick a sequencing approach for Dedicated vs Private. customers keep asking for both. proposal: prioritize Dedicated capacity for Q3 to hit throughput SLAs, then Private in Q4 with a narrow‑surface MVP. thoughts?
Mohit (Eng): I want data: do we have a RICE sketch for both options? impact huge for regulated customers with Private, but effort and risk are higher.
Jen (Product): agreed. my rough notes: Dedicated = high impact for current top 10 customers (throughput+SLA), low infra complexity (we already run similar). Private = high revenue per seat but long sales cycle.
Samir (Infra): ops perspective: Dedicated scale paths are well understood — autoscale rules, placement. Private needs VPC mesh, KMS, on‑prem packaging. estimate: Private adds ~4wk integration + 2 engineers for 3 months.
Alexa (PM): I made a quick RICE stub, nothing fancy. posting here:```
Option | Reach | Impact(1-10) | Confidence(%) | Effort(pts)
Dedicated | 4k requests/mo | 7 | 80 | 5
Private MVP | 200 seats | 8 | 50 | 13
```
Mohit (Eng): nice. if we convert to RICE score roughly (R*I*C)/E: Dedicated ≈ (4000*7*0.8)/5 = 4480, Private ≈ (200*8*0.5)/13 = 61.5 — huge delta but reach metric is apples vs oranges.
Maria (Sales): please don't bury reach. those 200 seats are enterprise deals with multi-year contracts. revenue impact per seat is 50x a standard hosted account.
Jen (Product): we should normalize to revenue‑weighted reach or split the scoring into near-term (Q3) vs strategic (12‑18mo). otherwise RICE skews to surface features.
Samir (Infra): also consider operational risk — Private has higher support cost and onboarding touch. we ought to include runbook effort as ongoing cost in the effort term.
Alexa (PM): proposed sequencing: 1) Q3 — expand Dedicated capacity + SLA packaging + simplified customer isolation features (soft isolation) 2) Q4 — Private MVP targeting 2 regulated customers with a narrow feature set (VPC + KMS + audit logs) 3) Q1 next year — expand Private automation and on‑prem installer.
Mohit (Eng): I'm +1 but want launch criteria: Dedicated considered "done" when sustained 95th pct latency < X ms at committed QPS and can autoscale without >5% error spike. Private MVP "done" when deployed to 2 customers without manual infra change and documented install < 3 days.
Jen (Product): can we make the Private MVP scope measurable: no custom kernels, only supported models from catalog, telemetry via customer opt‑in. keeps engineering bounded.
Maria (Sales): that scope is acceptable to the pilot customers. they asked for KMS + audit logs + SLA for data isolation; they don't need on‑prem floor support initially.
Alexa (PM): tallying constraints: technical effort, sales lead time, revenue per deal, support ops. next step: prioritize Dedicated in roadmap sprint, spin up a Private pilot workstream with 2 engs + 1 infra for Q4.
OpsBot: reminder — please create a product PRD checklist in #eng‑releases and tag @oncall two weeks before canary.
Mohit (Eng): I'll draft the PRD and include a simple RACI and rollback plan. aiming to post by EOD Friday.
Jen (Product): I'll align with sales for pilot customers and capture acceptance criteria.
Alexa (PM): thanks all. if nobody objects by EOD I'll lock the sequencing and we can publish a short note for execs. :white_check_mark:
Maria (Sales): ok from me. we should also flag any legal/regulatory needs early.
Samir (Infra): noted. I'll list infra deps and an approximate effort tracker in the PRD.
